Q: How do I make a flat list out of a list of lists? A:

From python 3.15, you can use unpacking in list comprehension as proposed and later accepted in PEP 798

lists = [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5]]
[*l for l in lists]  # equivalent to [x for l in lists for x in l]

Q: Google Maps markers become very slow when adding more than 1000 markers – how to optimize? A:

The performance lag happens because the google.maps.Data layer and standard DOM-based SVG icons are not optimized for continuously re-rendering thousands of points on state changes. Doing so heavily bottlenecks the browser's main thread.

To resolve this, you may apply one of these standard optimizations depending on your volume:

  1. Marker Clustering (1k - 50k markers)
    • Instead of rendering every point, group nearby markers into a single icon that expands upon zooming. Use the official @googlemaps/markerclusterer library to drastically reduce the number of elements the browser has to draw.
  2. WebGL Rendering via Deck.gl (Massive datasets)
    • If you must render all points simultaneously without clustering, you need to offload the rendering to the GPU. Use the WebGL Overlay View integrated with Deck.gl to handle hundreds of thousands of points smoothly.
  3. The Official React Library
    • Since you are using React, consider migrating to @vis.gl/react-google-maps. It is the officially sponsored library and handles map lifecycles and large datasets far better than custom useEffect hooks.

If the above solutions do not meet your exact use case, you can just file a Feature Request directly with the Google Maps Platform engineering team via the Public Issue Tracker.

Q: Whatever happened to Fredrik Lundh's Tkinter Construction Kit tkinter3000? A:

Fredrik Lundh, sadly, passed away in 2021, although, as you have noticed, the project had not received any updates for quite some time before.

So while I do not really know about tkinter3000 or the Tkinter Widget Construction Kit, I would conclude that what happened is the fate of many open-source projects: a project that was maintained by a small number of maintainers (I guess, one, in this case), at some point, did not see any new contributions and thus stalled.

Q: Calculating percentages for discrete values entered in an Excel column A:

Here is the simplest way using the GROUPBY function. The LAMBDA inside GROUPBY's function argument allows you to use two variables: the first represents each unique row field (each_letter), and the second represents the total number of values (all_rows). Wrap each argument in the COUNTA function and divide them.

=GROUPBY(
    A2:A11,
    A2:A11,
    LAMBDA(each_letter, all_rows, COUNTA(each_letter) / COUNTA(all_rows)),
    ,
    0
)

Q: Using MSSQL STUFF in query with PHP A:

Try this SQL call instead.

select invoice_id, [Total Paid] RefNumCount,PayCount, MIN([rowNumber]) as rowNumber, 
       Vendor, Due, [Invoice Number], Company, MAX(Location) as Location,
       SUM([Funded Amount]) as [Funded Amount], [Company ID], [Invoice ID],
       provider_reference_number, reconcile_date, all_providers , 
       STUFF((select '|' + t1.[Container Name]
              from @t t1
              where t1.[Invoice Number] = t.[Invoice Number]
              order by t1.[Container Name]
              for XML PATH('')),1,1,'') as [Container Name] 
from @t t
group by invoice_id, [Total Paid], RefNumCount, PayCount, Vendor, Due, [Invoice Number], 
         Company, [Company ID], [Invoice ID], provider_reference_number, reconcile_date, 
         all_providers

The error occured when you added '|' at the select statement below which will strip away the xml tags, causing error when you use .value() trying to extract the data.

STUFF((select '|' + ... from ... for XML PATH(''), TYPE).value('.', 'nvarchar(100)'),1,1,'')
